scope.notes: Inventory now totals 487 rows across five source books. The base 252 rows cover Exalted: The Sidereals character-creation overview (Chapter Three), the five Auspicious-Ability groups tied to the celestial constellations and their Celestial Hierarchy minimums, the universal caste-agnostic Anima Effect, all five Castes (Journeys, Serenity, Battles, Secrets, Endings) with their Anima Banners/Anima Effects/Caste Abilities/Associations/Sobriquets/Concepts, the Arcane Fate signature trait mechanic and its Sidereal Anima Banner visibility/Paradox table, the Craft (Fate) Ability specialty, the new/altered Backgrounds (Allies, Artifact, Backing, Familiar, Manse altered; Acquaintances, Celestial Manse, Connections, Salary, Savant, Sifu new), Chapter Five's general Charm framework (Manipulating Fate, Creatures Outside of Fate, Restricted Charms, Unusual Charms, Matters of Personality, Prayer Strips, Spotting Active Prayer Strips, On Memory, Presentation Format), all five Castes' full sets of Ability-line Charm trees (completing all 25 of Chapter Five's Caste-and-Ability Charm trees: Journeys 29 Charms, Serenity 30 Charms, Battles 31 Charms, Secrets 32 Charms, Endings 30 Charms including the Violet Bier of Sorrows Style), the general 'Sidereal Martial Arts' secret-style framework (including the Sutras resonance mechanic), and all three of the book's named secret Sidereal Martial Arts styles in full: Charcoal March of Spiders (12 Charms), Prismatic Arrangement of Creation (16 Charms), and Citrine Poxes of Contagion (13 Charms plus its tree-overview and Infectious Martial Arts/Spiritual Diseases framework rows), pp. 184-201/PDF 187-204. Also covers the Sidereal Astrology (Colleges/constellations) system in full: the rules framework (overview, Petitions paperwork, the Effect Roll procedure, Blessing/Curse effect types, Scope/Duration/Power tables, Multiple/Canceling Effects, Censure, Paradox, Pattern Bite), Resplendent Destinies (p. 215/PDF 218), the Procedure-and-Catalog-of-Colleges lead-in, and the full named-College catalog itself -- all five College Houses (Journeys, Leisure, War, Secrets, Endings, pp. 220-235/PDF 223-238) and the five Greater Signs (p. 235/PDF 238) that close Chapter Six. Also adds three Terrestrial/Celestial Circle sorcery spells cross-referenced from the Charm framework (Open the Spirit Door, Gift of Knowledge, Summoning the Heavenly Portal) and one Specialized Prayer (Prayer of the Chosen), pp. 122-124/PDF 125-127. A dedicated Merits/Flaws check found none: this book (and Exalted 1e generally) has no discrete Merits & Flaws system distinct from the standard Background/Virtue/Charm framework already inventoried. Chapter Seven onward (Storytelling/setting material) has not been reviewed. A second/third pass then triaged the cross-splat sorcery/artifice supplements Savant and Sorcerer and Book of Three Circles, adding 220 more rows (see below); a final, fourteenth pass then rendered and read the entire Sidereal portion of the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's Chapter Two ('The Celestial Exalted,' printed pp. 34-41/PDF 35-42) -- mostly narrative on post-Usurpation Sidereal society (Castes, the Immaculate Order relationship, Loom of Fate/Fate-weaving culture) -- and confirmed its only mechanical content, four 'Sample Charms' (Force Decision, Absence, Wise Choice, Prior Warning, all four on the same page, printed p. 41/PDF 42, immediately before the Abyssal Exalted section begins) are exact verbatim reprints of Charms already inventoried from Chapter Five of the core book (identical name, cost, duration, and mechanics), so no new rows were added for them; each pre-existing row's notes field was updated to cite this reprint. This book was added to the sources list below purely for that citation trail, even though it contributed zero new rows, keeping totalRows at 472. A quick skim of Chapter One ('The Scarlet Empire,' printed pp. 8-25/PDF 9-26) and Chapter Three ('Spirits and Spirit Courts,' printed pp. 48-75/PDF 49-76) found only Dragon-Blooded sample Charms (out of scope) and Spirit/demon NPC stat blocks respectively -- no player-facing Sidereal (or Lunar) exceptions in either chapter. the complete Chapter Five Terrestrial and Celestial Circle spell catalog (84 selectable spells, confirmed complete against the previous session's work), a 102-entry Hearthstone catalog (15 Sample Hearthstones from Savant and Sorcerer's Chapter Three plus 87 more from Book of Three Circles' Chapter Six 'long roll,' the latter explicitly not reprinted in Savant and Sorcerer per its own intro sidebar), a 13-row Artifice and Enchantment catalog from Savant and Sorcerer Chapter Two (the Artifact-rating framework, Drawback/alternate-power-source rules, the five-step creation process, Sidereal-specific creation notes, two named Merits, the Magical Materials catalog, exotic-ingredients examples, and 5 named Sample Artifacts including Soul Mirror), a 13-row Warstriders appendix (the overview/operation/benefits-limitations/maintenance framework, all five warstrider design classes as selectable Artifact-rated equipment, the weaponry-mounting/mundane-weapons/artifact-weapons reference catalogs, and the Proteus Gauntlet artifact), and an 8-row skim of Chapter One (Magical Theory: the Limits of Sorcery, the Black and White Treatises, the Five Unavoidable Challenges initiation framework, and Sidereal-specific initiation notes) and Chapter Four (Practical Summonings: the demon/elemental summoning overview, social/political/licensing context, mass summoning rules, and the Bound Spirit Limit Profile system), all bundled into GM-facing or reference-only rows given their non-selectable, Storyteller-procedural nature. See rulesNotes for the full citation trail.

Its Solar Circle sorcery chapter (Ch4) is out of scope for Sidereals.

Cross-splat sourcebook (image-based PDF, rendered page-by-page); Chapter Two's embedded Sidereal Charms are Sidereal-specific. Chapter Four's universal, cross-splat artifact catalog ('Further Wonders,' printed pp. 77-80/PDF 78-81: Ghost Cestus, Sling Bow of Ice, The Golden Viper, Land Ship, Singing Staff, Eye of Autochthon) was transcribed into Lunar's inventory as the master copy and has now also been derived into this inventory as a second master-copy set (same id/name/mechanics/cost/citation, notes flagged as derived) since no splat-specific restriction excludes Sidereal.

Cross-splat naval/nautical sourcebook (image-based PDF, rendered page-by-page); Chapter Four's 'Artifacts of the Waves' section (printed pp. 123-127/PDF 124-128) is a universal, non-splat-restricted catalog of naval artifacts, transcribed here in full. Its earlier 'Magics of the Sea' Charms section (printed pp. 114-122/PDF 115-123) is explicitly Solar/Dragon-Blooded-only per the book's own text and remains out of scope for Sidereal.
Universal Merits & Flaws chapter (Chapter One), applicable across all Exalted types including Sidereals

rulesNotes: Printed page numbers in this book run 3 less than the PDF page number supplied (PDF page = printed page + 3) for the copy used to build this inventory. Confirmed consistently across Chapter Three: Character Creation (PDF pp. 99-103, printed pp. 96-100) and Chapter Four: Traits (PDF pp. 107-127, printed pp. 104-124); both page numbers are recorded on every citation.
This PDF is image-based (no selectable text layer); all rows below were transcribed from rendered page images, per the 'OCR is an extraction aid, never verification by itself' rule.

Sidereals do not have a Limit Trait. Unlike Abyssal Resonance, their signature trait mechanic (Arcane Fate) is not a numeric, rated Trait with discrete gain/loss procedures -- it is a passive, always-on effect every Sidereal has from Exaltation onward. It is inventoried as a single mechanic row plus its associated Sidereal Anima Banner visibility/Paradox table, rather than as gain/loss/manifestation rows the way Resonance was for Abyssal.

The Sidereal Curse (the Great Curse's Sidereal-specific expression) is confirmed to be a roleplaying-only element with no discrete mechanical trigger or penalty table of its own (Chapter Three, PDF p. 103/printed p. 100 sidebar: 'The Sidereal Curse has no mechanical aspect and is, instead, a matter entirely for roleplaying. See page 253 of the Storytelling chapter for more information.'). It is therefore out of scope for this core-mechanics pass; no row was created for it.

Resplendent Destinies (referenced repeatedly from the Arcane Fate section as the means by which a Sidereal can bypass her own Arcane Fate and don a memorable identity) are detailed in full on pp. 215-218 of this book, which have not been rendered or reviewed in this pass. Only the cross-cutting interaction described within the in-scope Arcane Fate section itself (PDF pp. 124-125) is captured here; the full Resplendent Destiny system is out of scope for this inventory.

docs/references/exalted1e/dragon-blooded/source-manifest.json already cites this same book once for a single externally-sourced Dragon-Blooded spell (Open the Spirit Door, Terrestrial Circle Sorcery, PDF p. 125-126/printed p. 122-123), flagged 'external-source' because this Sidereals PDF had not been supplied at the time. That citation was not modified or duplicated here; it remains Dragon-Blooded catalog content.

Confirmed the printed-page-equals-PDF-minus-3 offset continues to hold in Chapter Five (Charms and Martial Arts, starting printed p. 128/PDF 131), by cross-checking the printed folio numbers embedded in the rendered page images against the PDF page numbers used to render them.

Chapter Five's Charm material is organized very differently from the other four splats reviewed so far: rather than grouping Charms by Attribute or a small number of thematic trees, it presents one Charm tree per Caste-and-Auspicious-Ability combination (5 Castes x 5 Auspicious Abilities = 25 trees total), each opened by a short poetic 'Scripture of the (Maiden)' epigraph and a named tree title (e.g. 'Endurance -- The Mast' for Journeys Caste). This inventory has so far completed one full tree (Journeys: Endurance) as a template for the remaining 24; each will need the same page-by-page treatment.

A few rows in this round have mechanics text that reads ambiguously in the source and were paraphrased as faithfully as possible rather than smoothed over: the exact numeric difficulty-by-range table for Spotting Active Prayer Strips was not transcribed row-by-row, and the healing-rate wording in One Direction Invocation's description is confusingly phrased in the book itself. Both are flagged in their own row's notes for a closer re-read before promotion.

The Journeys Caste's remaining four Charm trees (Ride 'The Messenger', Sail 'The Captain', Survival 'The Ship's Wheel', Thrown 'The Gull') are now complete, closing out the full Journeys Caste at pp. 134-142/PDF 137-145. Several Charm descriptions span a tree-diagram page break in the source (stat block on one page, prose on the next); these were transcribed as single continuous Charms with a note on the page split. Adopting the Untamed Face's row cross-references Exalted: The Lunars' ikth-ya/murr-ya Lunar social-caste terminology, which is out of scope for this inventory and not independently verified here.

The Serenity Caste (Craft 'The Peacock', Dodge 'The Ewer', Linguistics 'The Pillar', Performance 'The Musician', Socialize 'The Lovers', pp. 143-153/PDF 146-156) and the Battles Caste (Archery 'The Quiver', Brawl 'The Gauntlet', Melee 'The Spear', Presence 'The Banner', Resistance 'The Shield', pp. 153-162/PDF 156-165) are now both complete, closing out two full Castes.

The Secrets Caste (Investigation 'The Key', Larceny 'The Guardians', Lore 'The Treasure Trove', Occult 'The Sorcerer' in two parts, Stealth 'The Mask', pp. 163-173/PDF 166-176) is now complete, closing out a third full Caste beyond Journeys and matching the same per-Ability tree format. Occult is unusual in presenting two separate tree diagrams under one Ability ('The Sorcerer I', a Charm-based branch, and 'The Sorcerer II', which grants access to Terrestrial/Celestial Circle sorcery); both are treated as one combined Ability-line tree for this count. Auspicious Prospects for (Caste) (Investigation tree) is a single Charm presented as five near-identical Maiden-specific variants; the source text explicitly names variants for Journeys, Serenity, Battles, and Fate (Secrets) but does not explicitly name an Endings variant, which is flagged in that row's notes rather than guessed. Terrestrial Circle Sorcery's stat block prints an apparently inconsistent 'Duration: Simple' value, transcribed as printed and flagged in that row's notes.

Only the Endings Caste's five Ability-line Charm trees remain uninventoried to complete all 25 of Chapter Five's Charm trees. The Endings Caste header ('Endings: The Violet Bier of Sorrows') and its first tree (Athletics, 'The Rising Smoke') begin at printed p. 174/PDF 177, immediately after Secrets Caste's Stealth tree ends; its second tree (Awareness, 'The Crow') begins at printed p. 175/PDF 178. Resume point for the next round: printed p. 175/PDF 178, partway through the Awareness tree (Prior Warning and Expected Pain charms already identified but not yet checked in).

The Endings Caste's five Ability-line Charm trees (Athletics 'The Rising Smoke', Awareness 'The Crow', Bureaucracy 'The Haywain', Martial Arts 'The Sword' (the Violet Bier of Sorrows Style, also called the Endings Form), and Medicine 'The Corpse', pp. 174-184/PDF 177-187) are now complete, closing out the fifth and final Caste and all 25 of Chapter Five's Caste-and-Ability Charm trees. The Martial Arts tree is this book's first Ability-line tree built around a dedicated Martial Arts style rather than a mundane Ability; a sidebar on printed p. 179/PDF 182 ('Staff and Blade') specifies that its Charms treat knife, sword, staff, seven-section-staff, and serpent-sting-staff attacks as unarmed attacks and that none of its Charms function while wearing armor, folded into the root Charm's (Secrets of Future Strife) notes rather than given its own row. Immediately after this tree, the book opens a general 'Sidereal Martial Arts' section (printed p. 184/PDF 187) describing further secret styles available to Sidereals specifically (Charcoal March of Spiders, Prismatic Arrangement of Creation, Citrine Pox of Contagion) — these are a distinct system from the 25 Caste-and-Ability trees and remain unrendered/uninventoried; Charcoal March of Spiders' tree diagram and framework text (but not yet its Charm-by-Charm mechanics) have been rendered as of this pass. Resume point for the next round: printed p. 185/PDF 188, at the start of Charcoal March of Spiders Style's Charm descriptions (Unnatural Many-Step Stride).

A ninth pass added the general 'Sidereal Martial Arts' framework (sidereal-martial-arts, covering the three secret styles' shared framing) and its Sutras resonance mechanic (sidereal-martial-arts-sutras), then completed the entire Charcoal March of Spiders Style (12 Charms plus its tree-overview row, pp. 185-190/PDF 188-193): three roots (Unnatural Many-Step Stride, Maw of Dripping Venom, Rain of Unseen Threads) feeding Dance of the Hungry Spider, Charcoal March of Spiders Form, and Nest of Living Strands, converging through Cannibalistic Heritage Technique on Jumping Spider Strike, which spreads to Thumbnail Spider March and Water Spider Bite and the capstone Grandmother Spider Mastery via Pattern Spider Touch. The pass then began Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Style (a 16-Charm tree built around the Five Magical Materials, pp. 190-191/PDF 193-194), completing its tree-overview row, its four root Charms (Deadly Starmetal Offensive, Orichalcum Sheathing Stance, Flickering Moonsilver Approach, Five Jade Fury) and its first Form Charm (Four Magical Materials Form, converging all four roots). Resume point for the next round: printed p. 191/PDF 194, continuing Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Style past Four Magical Materials Form (11 Charms remain in that tree), then Citrine Pox of Contagion Style (not yet located/rendered).

A tenth pass finished the rest of Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Style's 16-Charm tree (pp. 191-194/PDF 194-197): Four Magical Materials Form's two branches -- Charm Redirection Technique feeding Sequential Charm Disruption and Spell-Shattering Palm, and Astrology Interruption Method feeding Soul Fire Shaper Form -- converge (with Demesne Emulation Practice's Demesne and Manse Form) via God Ways/(Type) Exalt Ways and Games of Divinity Form on the capstone Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Form. It then located and fully inventoried the book's third and final named secret Sidereal Martial Arts style, Citrine Poxes of Contagion (pp. 195-201/PDF 198-204; note the book consistently spells it plural, 'Poxes,' not the singular 'Pox'): its tree-overview row and a separate Infectious Martial Arts/Spiritual Diseases framework row (covering the Mundane/Magical Treatment Difficulty system and the three Circles of spiritual illness severity), then all 13 Charms across two linked tree diagrams -- first diagram: Feverish Essence Discharge Atemi, Disjointed Essence Infectious Atemi, and Convulsive Displacement Infectious Atemi (three infectious-atemi roots) converging on Essence-Disrupting Infectious Atemi, alongside Perfect Reconstruction Method and Spirit and Body Purification Touch (two curative roots) converging on Flare of Invulnerability Method, with Spirit and Body Purification Touch also feeding Inner Dragon Unbinding, all three branches converging on the Form Charm Citrine Poxes of Contagion Form; second diagram: that Form feeds Spiritual Perfection, which feeds both Gentle Touch of the Wicked Hand and Glorious Sidereal Protection, converging on the capstone Essence-Shattering Typhoon. This closes out all three of the book's named secret Sidereal Martial Arts styles (Charcoal March of Spiders, Prismatic Arrangement of Creation, Citrine Poxes of Contagion). Resume point for the next round: printed p. 202/PDF 205 is a full-page illustration with no Charm content; the full Colleges/astrology system, Resplendent Destinies (pp. 215-218), and a check for Sidereal-specific Merits/Flaws all remain unrendered/uninventoried and their exact page locations within the remainder of the book (printed pp. 202-253+) have not yet been confirmed by rendering.

An eleventh pass located and inventoried the Sidereal Astrology (Colleges/constellations) rules system, printed pp. 204-218/PDF 207-221: the section overview (sidereal-astrology-overview), Petitions (the paperwork/calligraphy/co-and-countersignature procedure for casting an astrology effect), the Effect Roll (Determining, Formulating, and Activating Effects), the Blessing/Curse Effect Types split, the Effect Scope/Duration/Power tables, rules for Multiple Effects and Canceling Effects, Censure (the penalty for illicit/unauthorized astrology use), Paradox (astrology's equivalent to sorcerous backlash), and Pattern Bite (a lingering-consequence mechanic). Resplendent Destinies (resplendent-destinies, printed p. 215/PDF 218) was also inventoried as a single calculated row covering the full system (not just the earlier cross-reference from the Arcane Fate section). The pass then opened the 'Procedure for Sidereal Astrology and Catalog of Colleges' section (sidereal-astrology-procedure-and-catalog-overview, printed p. 218/PDF 221), which is the book's lead-in to the actual named-College catalog. Resume point for the next round: printed p. 218/PDF 221 (or the page immediately following, if that page is entirely the section's introductory text), continuing into the specific Colleges/constellations catalog itself -- the individual named Colleges (their Charm-tree-equivalent astrology-effect lists) have not yet been transcribed. A check for Sidereal-specific Merits/Flaws also remains outstanding.

A twelfth pass located and inventoried three Terrestrial/Celestial Circle sorcery spells cross-referenced from the Chapter Five Charm framework and Occult tree (Open the Spirit Door, Gift of Knowledge, Summoning the Heavenly Portal, printed pp. 122-124/PDF 125-127) and one Specialized Prayer (Prayer of the Chosen, printed pp. 123-124/PDF 126-127, automatically known by any Sidereal with two or more combined dots in Occult and Savant), then completed the full named-College catalog for the Sidereal Astrology system: the House of Journeys (The Captain, The Gull, The Mast, The Messenger, The Ship's Wheel; printed pp. 220-222/PDF 223-225, matching the Journeys Caste's five Auspicious Abilities one-for-one), the House of Leisure (The Ewer, The Lovers, The Musician, The Peacock, The Pillar; printed pp. 223-225/PDF 226-228, matching the Serenity Caste -- note the book names this house 'Leisure,' not 'Serenity'), the House of War (The Banner, The Gauntlet, The Quiver, The Shield, The Spear; printed pp. 226-228/PDF 229-231, matching the Battles Caste -- the book names this house 'War,' not 'Battles'), the House of Secrets (The Guardians, The Key, The Mask, The Sorcerer, The Treasure Trove; printed pp. 228-230/PDF 231-233, matching the Secrets Caste; the Mask is explicitly the college damaged by the post-Purge Arcane Fate, so Sidereals cannot self-target its ascending/descending effects), and the House of Endings (The Corpse, The Crow, The Haywain, The Rising Smoke, The Sword; printed pp. 231-235/PDF 234-238, matching the Endings Caste), plus the five Greater Signs of the Maidens (Mercury/Travel, Venus/Serenity, Mars/War, Jupiter/Secrets, Saturn/Endings; printed p. 235/PDF 238) that close Chapter Six. This closes out the entire Sidereal Astrology system and all 25 Colleges (five houses x five colleges each, one-to-one with the 25 Caste-and-Ability Charm trees from Chapter Five). Each house was inventoried as a single reference-only row (matching the House of Journeys template) rather than one row per college, given the volume of near-identical Trappings/Correlations/Resplendent-Effect prose; ascending/descending write-ups and Resplendent Effects are paraphrased rather than verbatim throughout. A dedicated Merits/Flaws search covered Chapter Three (Character Creation, printed pp. 94-101/PDF 97-104) and Chapter Four (Traits, printed pp. 102-125/PDF 105-128) and found no Sidereal-specific (or generic) Merits/Flaws system in this book; Exalted 1st Edition does not have a Merits & Flaws chapter comparable to later editions, so this is confirmed as a genuine absence rather than an unrendered section. This pass brings the inventory to 252 rows with no outstanding resume point within Chapters One through Six; Chapter Seven onward (Storytelling/setting material) was not reviewed, as it is out of scope for a Charm/mechanics inventory.

A thirteenth pass (a fresh session picking up after the prior one stalled on transient provider errors partway through the Chapter Five spell catalog) confirmed the 84 Terrestrial/Celestial Circle spell rows already added from Savant and Sorcerer Chapter Five (printed pp. 100-143/PDF 101-144) were complete by cross-checking every spell header in the rendered chapter against the inventory; no gaps were found (the apparent gap around PDF p. 121 turned out to be Charms of an automaton embedded within The Spy Who Walks in Darkness's own spell entry, not standalone spells). It then added the Hearthstone catalog: 15 Sample Hearthstones from Savant and Sorcerer Chapter Three (printed pp. 46-49/PDF 47-50, three per level across Levels One through Five, including an Abyssal-flavored Level Four stone, The Ice Gem), then -- since that book's own intro explicitly states it does not reprint the Hearthstone 'long roll' -- rendered and transcribed Book of Three Circles Chapter Six's image-based Hearthstone catalog (87 more entries, prefixed hearthstone-botc-* where a name/effect collided with an already-inventoried Savant and Sorcerer stone; exact-duplicate reprints, such as the Snakeskin Stone, were skipped with a cross-reference note on the original entry instead of being re-added). All 102 Hearthstone rows are selectable and cross-referenced to the Manse Background. source-manifest.json's book-of-three-circles role text was updated to reflect that it is now the primary Hearthstone source rather than a fully-superseded gap-filler.

The same thirteenth pass then added a 13-row Artifice and Enchantment catalog from Savant and Sorcerer Chapter Two (printed pp. 23-44/PDF 24-45): four gm-only rules-framework rows (the Artifact rating framework covering Power/Usefulness/Game Impact/Script Immunity/Drawback; the Drawback-subtype and alternate-power-source rules; the five-step artifact creation process; and Sidereal-specific creation notes on starmetal scarcity and Bronze Faction/Yu-Shan workshop access), two selectable named Merits (Starting Workshop, Moonsilver Initiate), one reference-only Magical Materials catalog (Jade/Soulsteel/Moonsilver/Starmetal/Orichalcum, including the grim Sidereal-specific account of starmetal's true origin as an executed god's Essence), one gm-only Exotic Ingredients examples row, and five selectable Sample Artifacts (Collar of Dawn's Cleansing Light Artifact 1, Mask Artifact 2, Ring of Being Artifact 4, Wings of the Raptor Artifact 4, and Soul Mirror Artifact 5). It then added a 13-row Warstriders appendix from Savant and Sorcerer's Appendix (printed pp. 144-160/PDF 145-161): four gm-only/reference rules rows (overview and design classes, operation and Essence costs, benefits and limitations, and maintenance), the five basic warstrider design classes as selectable Artifact-rated equipment (Scout ***, Common ***, Noble ****, Royal *****, Juggernaut *****), and three more rows bundling the weaponry-mounting rules, the mundane weapon-stat tables, and the artifact weapon-stat tables as reference-only catalogs, plus the Proteus Gauntlet (Artifact 4) as a selectable named artifact. Finally, a quick skim of Chapter One (Magical Theory, printed pp. 7-19/PDF 8-20) and Chapter Four (Practical Summonings, printed pp. 71-99/PDF 72-100) surfaced only Storyteller-facing or setting-flavor content -- four rows from Chapter One (the Limits of Sorcery, the Black and White Treatises acquisition mechanic, the Five Unavoidable Challenges initiation framework, and Sidereal-specific initiation notes) and four bundled rows from Chapter Four (the demon/elemental summoning-procedure overview, social/political/licensing context, mass summoning project rules, and the 10-archetype Bound Spirit Limit Profile system used to run captured spirits as NPCs) were added as gm-only or reference-only, deliberately not broken into dozens of per-archetype or per-table rows given their non-selectable, purely procedural nature. This pass brings the inventory to 472 rows; no outstanding resume point remains for Savant and Sorcerer or Book of Three Circles within Sidereal scope (Book of Three Circles' Chapter Four Solar Circle sorcery remains explicitly out of scope, as Sidereals do not have Solar Circle Sorcery access).

A fourteenth pass rendered and read the entire Sidereal portion of the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's Chapter Two ('The Celestial Exalted'), confirmed to run from printed p. 34/PDF 35 to printed p. 41/PDF 42 (Chapter Three, 'Spirits and Spirit Courts,' begins on printed p. 48/PDF 49; the Abyssal Exalted section of Chapter Two sits between the Sidereal section and Chapter Three). This section is almost entirely narrative on post-Usurpation Sidereal society (the five Castes' social roles, the fraught Immaculate Order relationship, Loom of Fate/Fate-weaving culture) with no new Charms or mechanics of its own. Its only mechanical content is a 'Sample Charms' sidebar (all four on the same page, printed p. 41/PDF 42) presenting Force Decision, Absence, Wise Choice, and Prior Warning as illustrative examples for Storytellers -- all four are exact verbatim reprints (identical name, cost, duration, and mechanics) of Charms already inventoried from this book's own Chapter Five, so no new rows were added; each pre-existing row's notes field was instead updated to cite this second appearance. exalted-storytellers-companion was added to the sources list above purely for that citation trail; totalRows remained 472 at the time (unchanged) since that pass added zero new rows. The same pass then quickly skimmed Chapter One ('The Scarlet Empire,' printed pp. 8-25/PDF 9-26) and Chapter Three ('Spirits and Spirit Courts,' printed pp. 48-75/PDF 49-76) per this project's cross-splat-exception-check convention: Chapter One (pp. 9-16 pure narrative; pp. 16-26 Dragon-Blooded Sample Charms, explicitly out of scope for Sidereal/Lunar) and Chapter Three (elemental/spirit-court NPC stat blocks and Charms throughout, all GM/Storyteller material) both yielded no player-facing exceptions relevant to Lunar or Sidereal characters. A fifteenth pass then added two small universal artifact catalogs, bringing the inventory to 487 rows. First, six rows (artifact-ghost-cestus, artifact-sling-bow-of-ice, artifact-the-golden-viper, artifact-land-ship, artifact-singing-staff, artifact-eye-of-autochthon) were derived, not independently re-read, from Lunar's already-verified transcription of the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's Chapter Four ('Further Wonders,' printed pp. 77-80/PDF 78-81), a universal cross-splat artifact catalog explicitly recorded there as a master copy for exactly this kind of derivation; each row keeps the same id/name/mechanics/cost/citation as the Lunar master row and adds a Sidereal-specific note flagging it as derived. All six carried over cleanly: none of their compatibility text names any restriction that would exclude Sidereal (Ghost Cestus, Sling Bow of Ice, Land Ship, Singing Staff, and Lightning-style Golden Viper/Eye of Autochthon rows all say 'any Exalt,' 'any owner,' or 'any possessor'), so no row was skipped. Second, eight named-artifact rows plus one reference-only summary table (artifact-cargo-preservation-spindles, artifact-armor-of-aquatic-puissance, artifact-steelsilk-sails, artifact-storm-sapphire, artifact-cord-of-winds, artifact-wavecleaver-daiklaive, artifact-light-implosion-bow, artifact-ship-weapons-table, artifact-lightning-ballista) were freshly transcribed from the Savage Seas sourcebook's Chapter Four 'Artifacts of the Waves' naval artifact catalog (printed pp. 123-127/PDF 124-128, the entire catalog through the last content page before the back cover on PDF p. 129), read from rendered page images since this PDF has no text layer. All nine rows are naval/nautical equipment kept selectable (except the reference-only summary table) with no splat-specific restriction excluding Sidereal noted anywhere in the source. This closes out the entire 'Artifacts of the Waves' section; the book's earlier 'Magics of the Sea' Charms section (printed pp. 114-122/PDF 115-123) is explicitly Solar/Dragon-Blooded-only per the book's own text and remains out of scope for Sidereal, so it was not transcribed.
